# Home Assistant integration for UniFi Drive / UNAS v0.7.1 - Discovery write-throttle hardening

Maintenance release focused on recorder and config-entry write hygiene.

## Highlights

- Throttles metadata-only discovery identity writes so repeated observations do
  not persist `discovery_last_seen` on every short-interval trigger.
- Applies the same write-throttle behavior to config-flow discovery matching and
  setup-time validated identity updates.
- Fixes the frontend setup race that could show `Invalid flow specified` after
  submitting `UniFi Drive optional features` even though the entry was created.
- Allows Home Assistant-managed device entries for this integration to be
  removed without a restart cycle.
- Adds direct unit coverage for discovery write decisions, including invalid
  timestamp handling and repeated discovery dedupe behavior.

## Live DB probe summary

A live Home Assistant test run on this branch validated the write-throttle
behavior:

- idle interval (`30s`): no config-entry write touch
- reload cycle 1 (`+30s`): one config-entry touch (expected first write in
  window)
- reload cycle 2 (`+30s`): no config-entry touch
- reload cycle 3 (`+30s`): no config-entry touch

The integration still writes normal entity state updates on explicit reloads,
but repeated short-window discovery metadata updates no longer churn config
entry storage.

## Validation

- `python scripts/check_repo.py`
- `python -m pytest -q`
- `python -m compileall -q custom_components/unifi_unas tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `ruff check custom_components tests scripts` (executed in an isolated local venv)
